description:
Measured while landing fz-kdt.104 (which dropped the arms a sibling COULD
stand in for). What is left is the harder half of the same defect:
dispatch arms whose runtime questions are literally the same question,
where NO arm semantically covers the others, so no arm can be dropped
without losing a body.

MEASURED AT FIFO, 577-fixture corpus, post-fz-kdt.104 (instrumented run
of callsite_dispatch::call_destinations): 12 distinct dispatch shapes
across 10 fixtures, 18 indistinguishable arm pairs. Two sub-shapes:

(1) NO QUESTIONS AT ALL (8 shapes: 00231_joined_fn_refs_enum_reduce,
00275_enum_count_member_reduce, 00277_enum_tier0_fixture,
00281_opaque_reducer_closure, behavior/enum_map_family,
behavior/opaque_fn_value_join, behavior/range_enumerable,
behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2). The arms differ only in
closure IDENTITY at some position; runtime_type_test_envelope collapses
funcs to fun_top, discriminating_inputs finds nothing, and the plan is a
bare source-order fallthrough. This is the documented
callable-correlation policy (callsite_dispatch.rs test
callable_flow_dispatch_does_not_discriminate_unobservable_callable_correlations,
and compiler2/dispatch_reachability agreeing with source-ordered
selection), so it may be correct-by-policy rather than a defect -- but
nobody has PROVEN the first arm is always the right one, and it is arm
order deciding semantics.

(2) REAL QUESTIONS THAT CANNOT SEPARATE (4 shapes:
00277_enum_tier0_fixture arms=3, behavior/enum_map_family arms=3,
behavior/enum_predicate_search arms=3,
behavior/fz_f98_range_map_converges arms=2). Example from 00277, one
callsite, three arms on the SAME function: surfaces
[:tail],[:tail],(...) / [int],[int],(...) / [{any,any}],[{any,any}],(...).
All three project to the same RuntimeTypePredicate -- 'a list' -- because
the predicate records list SHAPE (Empty/NonEmpty) and tuple ARITY only,
never element types. Source order alone routes every list to whichever
arm the scheduler happened to put first, and the three bodies are
different specializations (different lanes/reprs).

THIS TICKET NOW ALSO OWNS 00277'S RESIDUAL SCHEDULE GAP (re-homed from
fz-kdt.106 by its cold review, 2026-09-01): 00277's FIFO/LIFO canon gap
SURVIVES dominance absorption (1821 -> 500 lines, 178 vs 179
executables, deterministic across three runs) -- it is NOT ascent-history
chains (which absorption collapses) but a set of pairwise-incomparable
transient rows feeding exactly this ticket's 3-arm same-predicate
callsite. 00277 is removed from fz-kdt.106's acceptance lenses;
re-measure its residual after this ticket lands. NOTE: 00277's interp
run is truncated by fz-kdt.111, so behaviour claims about it must use
the JIT or AOT door (both verified byte-identical under absorption).

THE DIRECTION (do not start without review): fz-kdt.104's cure -- drop
the arm -- does not apply, because no arm's body covers the others. The
cure has to be the other side: either the runtime predicate learns to
answer the question the arms actually differ on (element-type/payload
discrimination is NOT free at runtime -- it is O(n) on a list), or the
analysis must not mint sibling specializations it cannot dispatch
between (join them at the callsite instead, one body for one runtime
question). Measure both before choosing. The FIFO/LIFO evidence for (2)
is unmeasured beyond 00277: check whether any of the four flips behavior
under Agenda::pop -> pop_back before pricing a cure.
title: Runtime-indistinguishable dispatch twins that no arm covers: the predicate cannot separate what analysis minted (12 shapes / 18 pairs post-104; owns 00277's residual schedule gap)
